metadata.summary: A dataset of 10,015 dermatoscopic images of pigmented skin lesions collected from two sources: a hospital-centered archive of the Department of Dermatology at the Medical University of Vienna, and a smaller public repository of the ISIC Archive.
metadata.custodian: Medical University of Vienna; International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC)
metadata.purpose: Intended as a training and benchmarking set for machine learning models for automated skin lesion classification; to meet the need for a publicly available standard benchmark.

papers.title: The HAM10000 dataset, a large collection of multi-source dermatoscopic images of common pigmented skin lesions

ethics.privacy_measures: Images were de-identified prior to release; no patient identifiers retained.

extraction.notes: Baseline card derived solely from dataset_catalog.xlsx real metadata; remaining fields require paper/README or manual completion.
pending_verification: The following LLM fields were auto-dropped for violating schema constraints and reverted to baseline; pending manual review: data_collection_setting, medical_fields[list-items]

known_limitations: Predominantly Austrian/European origin limits geographic and ethnic diversity.
Lack of detailed demographic metadata (age, sex, ethnicity) hinders subgroup analysis.
Potential selection bias toward lesions deemed clinically or diagnostically relevant.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: No synthetic data; minor preprocessing (e.g., cropping, resizing) applied for uniformity; no details on augmentation in source text.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: 90%+ images from Austria; underrepresentation of darker skin tones and non-European populations.
bias_and_limitations.long_tail_classes: Yes — class distribution is imbalanced (e.g., melanoma n=1113, vascular lesions n=115).
bias_and_limitations.generalizability_statement: Generalizability to non-European populations and diverse skin types is limited due to geographic and demographic skew.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic attributes (age, sex, ethnicity) are largely missing.

tasks_and_use.excluded_tasks: Not intended for detection or segmentation without additional annotation.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Collected from a hospital-centered archive (Medical University of Vienna) and a public repository (ISIC Archive) to create a large, multi-source benchmark for skin lesion classification.
data_origin.aggregation_multisource: Aggregated from two sources: hospital archive (majority) and ISIC public repository (minority); no details on stratification or rebalancing provided.

population.target_population: Patients with pigmented skin lesions undergoing dermatoscopic evaluation.
population.missing_groups: No explicit demographic subgroup statistics stated in the abstract; known underrepresentation of non-Caucasian skin types and non-European populations is widely reported in literature but not quantified in source text.

annotation.annotation_method: Diagnoses assigned by expert dermatologists; ground truth labels derived from histopathology, follow-up, or consensus of experts.
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from histopathology, follow-up, or consensus of experts.
annotation.label_noise_description: Label noise exists due to inter-observer variability and diagnostic uncertainty; some labels reflect clinical diagnosis rather than histopathological confirmation.
